skills.trigger: When evaluating a fetal thoracic mass on ultrasound to determine its impact on adjacent anatomy and distinguish between differential diagnoses like CPAM and bronchopulmonary sequestration.
steps: Identify the echogenicity and cystic nature of the lung lesion (e.g., multicystic mass) and assess for mass effect, specifically checking for mediastinal shift (heart displacement) and diaphragmatic position (elevation or depression).

Apply color Doppler to the lesion to identify the vascular supply; distinguish bronchopulmonary sequestration (systemic arterial supply from the aorta) from CPAM (pulmonary circulation), as this confirms the diagnosis and explains the space-occupying behavior causing the observed anatomical displacement.
